holidays.name: National Noodle Day
holidays.description: A slurp-worthy celebration of noodles in every form, from ramen and spaghetti to pad thai and lo mein. People mark the day by cooking, ordering, or simply twirling a big bowl of their favorite strands.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food observance popular in the United States, it is widely listed on October 6 in food holiday calendars. Its exact founder is unclear, as with many food days that spread through social media and calendar websites.
holidays.funFact: The oldest known noodles were found in China at the Lajia archaeological site and are about 4,000 years old. They were made from millet.

holidays.name: National German-American Day
holidays.description: A day honoring the contributions of German immigrants and their descendants to American culture, from pretzels and beer gardens to kindergartens and Christmas trees.
holidays.origin: It commemorates the October 6, 1683 arrival of the first group of German immigrants who landed in Philadelphia and founded Germantown, Pennsylvania. It was made an official annual observance by Congress and President Reagan in 1987.
holidays.funFact: Roughly 40 million Americans claim German ancestry, making it one of the largest ancestry groups in the United States.

holidays.name: Mad Hatter Day
holidays.description: A whimsical celebration inspired by the Mad Hatter from Alice's Adventures in Wonderland. Fans wear silly hats, throw tea parties, and embrace a bit of delightful nonsense.
holidays.origin: It was created in the early 2000s by Seattle-area fans of Lewis Carroll. The date is chosen because the Mad Hatter's hat carries a price tag reading 10/6, meaning 10 shillings and sixpence, as in the original illustrations by John Tenniel.
holidays.funFact: The Mad Hatter is never actually called that in the book. He is just called the Hatter, and the 'mad as a hatter' phrase is likely linked to mercury poisoning among 19th-century hat makers.

holidays.name: World Cerebral Palsy Day
holidays.description: A global awareness day that spotlights the more than 17 million people living with cerebral palsy. It encourages inclusion, accessibility, and celebration of people with the condition.
holidays.origin: It began in 2012 as a grassroots movement, started by Cerebral Palsy Alliance and a global network of organizations, to ensure people with cerebral palsy have the same rights, access, and opportunities as everyone else.
holidays.funFact: The official color for the day is green, and landmarks around the world light up in green to show support.

holidays.name: Physician Assistants Day
holidays.description: A day to thank the physician assistants who diagnose illnesses, assist in surgeries, and provide care across healthcare settings. Many clinics celebrate with treats and thank-you notes.
holidays.origin: National PA Day is held on October 6, chosen because it is the anniversary of the graduation of the first class of physician assistants from Duke University in 1967.
holidays.funFact: The PA profession was created in the 1960s, in part to put experienced military medics back to work in healthcare after returning from the Vietnam War.
